_note: Visible copy for the gateway and guide. Drafted on gcp-gemini-pro (HEARTH task cc-d556e077), then hand-corrected: no drones, no cryptography, no visitor counters, no 3D — only controls that exist on the live pages. Never use the words character or archetype. Era facts are never hard-coded here: the guide's era table is generated at build time. {{builders}}, {{photos}}, {{eras_with_photos}} are baked by build.py.

gateway.lede: Photographs of what people built on the Comfy Valheim server, era by era, credited from the saved world itself.
gateway.search_placeholder: Your Valheim name, or any name you have built under
gateway.search_hint: Any name you ever built under. Matching names alone never join two builders.
gateway.manual_lede: Five short paths through the archive. Each one names the real controls you will use.

steps: Type any name you have built under into the search box.
Pick your builder from the list to open your page.
Read the albums credited to you, era by era.

guide.lede: Every builder recorded on a saved construction piece has a page. Credits come from the world file, not from claims, so the list is complete even where no photograph exists yet.
walkthrough: Open the builders index and press Ctrl K, or click the search box, then type any name you have built under. Aliases count.
Suggestions appear as you type. Pick one to open that builder's page.
Use Sort and the era chips to narrow the index, or tick With albums to see only builders with photographed work.
On your page, each era lists the albums credited to you with piece counts, and the photographs taken of them.
Your page keeps a Top 8 of the people you built with most, worked out from the pieces you placed side by side.
If an album is yours, open it and choose I built this. The claim is written to this browser only.
Nothing leaves the browser until you copy the participation payload and pass it to a coordinator.

study.aria_label: Study how the builds were made
steps: Open the gallery and press Filters.
Narrow by kind of place, perspective, weather or structure.
Open a photograph and step through every shot of that build.

guide.h2: Study how the builds were made
guide.lede: The gallery is a grid of photographs with a filter panel. It is built for looking closely, one structure at a time.
walkthrough: Press Filters at the top left to open the panel. Facets cover era, region, perspective, kind of place, weather, area and structure.
Choose a perspective such as eye level or detail to see joinery and proportion rather than silhouettes.
Sort with the chips at the bottom of the panel: biggest build, tallest, by rank, newest, or starred first.
Set Page size to load more frames at once.
Click a photograph to open it. The Where you are breadcrumbs show the era, the area and the build.
Below the photograph, every shot of this build lets you orbit the same structure from each captured angle.

walk.aria_label: Walk the eras, one photograph at a time
steps: Start in the earliest era with photographs.
Use the era chips in the Filters panel to move forward in time.
Follow the breadcrumbs from a photograph back to its builder.

guide.lede: Each era is a world that was later wiped. The photographs are what remains. Start early and move forward to watch the server's building style change.
walkthrough: Begin in era 7, the earliest era with photographs.
Open Filters. The era chips at the top switch to any other era that has been photographed.
Some eras are still being photographed. Their builders are already in the index, and their albums fill in as captures land.
Open a photograph and use the Where you are breadcrumbs to jump to the surrounding area.
The builder named on a photograph links to their page, where the same album sits beside their work from other eras.

request.aria_label: Ask for new photographs of a build
steps: Open a builder's page and choose Request photo on an album.
Pick preset styles and add instructions.
Copy the payload and send it to a coordinator.

guide.h2: Ask for new photographs of a build
guide.lede: Capture sessions follow requests. A request is a small text payload that you copy and pass on. It is never sent on its own.
walkthrough: Find the builder in the index and open their page.
Choose Request photo on the album you have in mind. The Request additional photographs dialog opens.
Tick any of the five preset styles: wide overview, entry-level detail, interior signature shot, height variation, or evening tone study.
Add photograph instructions, an optional contact preference, and mark it urgent if it is.
Submit request writes it to Your participation on this device in this browser only.
Choose Copy participation payload and send the text to a coordinator. Forget my participation clears the browser record.

data.aria_label: Open the statistics and the raw data
steps: Fetch the same JSON files the pages read.
Explore the world itself in the world viewer.

guide.h2: Open the statistics and the raw data
guide.lede: Every page here is static. What the pages read, you can read. The files are plain JSON behind the same URLs.
walkthrough: The statistics page summarises builders, albums, photographs and eras across the archive.
The builders index reads directory.json; each builder page reads its own thread file.
Each era's gallery reads its own index.json, plus depth.json and judge.json where they exist.
Builder keys are opaque identifiers. Names are display text; the key is the identity.
The world viewer opens the saved worlds themselves, with the builds in place.

guide.aria_label: Not sure? Learn what each path is for

guide.lede: Five paths through the archive, the honest version of how claims and requests work, and where the data lives.

paragraphs: Credits on this site are derived from the saved world. A claim is a self-reported marker beside those credits, not a change to them.
When you choose I built this, or submit a photograph request, the record is written to this browser under Your participation on this device. Nothing is transmitted.
To finish, choose Copy participation payload and send the text to a coordinator. Forget my participation removes the record from this browser.

data.lede: The same JSON the pages fetch, at stable URLs.

files.what: Every builder: key, display name, aliases, eras, album, photo and piece counts, tier.
One builder's albums per era, with contributors and their piece shares, and the photographs of each album.
The current era and the list of era galleries.
One era's photographs with their facets. The current era lives at /valheim/.
Optional aesthetic scores used by the auto scored sort.

data.world_viewer: The world viewer opens the saved worlds with the builds in place.
